visualMetaphor: a moneylender's wooden bench snapped in two, its halves turning into a banknote torn down the middle
title: Why 'bankrupt' means 'broken bench'
angle: The bench-smashing story behind 'banca rotta' is probably figurative; the real record is harsher: England's 1706 act made hiding assets from creditors a hanging crime, and in 1761 John Perrott, a Ludgate Hill shopkeeper caught with torn halves of banknotes, was hanged for it. The same act created the discharge, the fresh start bankruptcy still means today.
